source.citation: Diggs, G.M., Lipscomb, B.L. & O'Kennon, R.J. (1999). Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.page_basis: Printed page in original flora; PDF leaf number equals printed page minus 209
source.source_access: Uploaded source PDF, page text inspected

method: Additive source-specific transcription/paraphrase only; untouched existing species.json, photos and BONAP distributions; null/omitted fields not stated by source

flora_morphology.habit: Aromatic woolly-pubescent rhizomatous perennial; 35–100 cm; flowering stem usually unbranched below inflorescence
flora_morphology.leaves: Alternate, sessile, lanceolate, 2–3 times pinnately compound; crowded narrow leaflets finely toothed or lobed
flora_morphology.heads: Small heads in dense terminal corymb
flora_morphology.rays: 5–12 white, rarely pinkish rays; ligules ca. 2 mm

disagreements_or_notes: Flora 5–12 rays versus FNA (3–)5–8 rays; both source-specific ranges retained
Native versus introduced lineages unresolved; no BONAP inference

external_crosscheck.finding: Ray florets (3–)5–8; literature describes variable complex; differs from regional flora's 5–12

records.flora_original_name: Acmella oppositifolia (Lam.) R.K. Jansen var. repens (Walter) R.K. Jansen

flora_morphology.habit: Rhizomatous perennial, creeping and rooting at nodes; ascending flowering branches
flora_morphology.leaves: Opposite, petiolate; blades ovate, rhombic to deltoid, 20–40 mm, serrate
flora_morphology.heads: Few solitary heads on axillary peduncles 5–15 cm
flora_morphology.rays: Few, yellow, pistillate but infertile; ligules ca. 5 mm
flora_morphology.receptacle: Paleae about equaling disc florets; elongate conic receptacle 8–10 mm in fruit
flora_morphology.fruits: Black achenes; pappus absent or rarely 1–2 awns

disagreements_or_notes: Original name at varietal rank; species-level matching supported by FNA; authorship spelling differs between current record and FNA, review before renaming

external_crosscheck.finding: FNA recognizes species as Acmella repens; historical regional name at varietal rank

flora_morphology.stems: Long spreading cottony hairs on stems and leaf margins
flora_morphology.leaves: Sessile, entire; lowest oblanceolate; upper ovate and clasping
flora_morphology.phyllaries: Approximately 2 slightly unequal rows, lanceolate, subappressed
flora_morphology.fruits: Achenes with cage-like exterior of stout separate ribs

disagreements_or_notes: Original flora lists Helenium setigerum as synonym; existing learner mentions short papery pappus but flora account does not document it: do not attribute that assertion to Diggs

flora_morphology.leaves: Opposite, sometimes uppermost alternate; pinnatifid to bipinnatifid, petioles usually 10–30 mm
flora_morphology.heads: Staminate short-stalked heads above separate pistillate heads
flora_morphology.fruits: Burr-like pistillate involucres ca. 3 mm, obovoid, subulate spines; key: 5–7 short spines

disagreements_or_notes: Record says upper leaves alternate generally; flora qualifies uppermost as sometimes alternate. Preserve variable character

flora_morphology.habit: Perennial forming colonies via creeping rootstocks; stems 0.3–0.6(–1+) m
flora_morphology.leaves: Sessile, pinnatifid; key contrasts with petiolate annual ragweed
flora_morphology.fruits: Burr-like fruits ca. 2.5 mm, obovoid, acute or blunt tubercles; key: 4–6 short stout tubercles

disagreements_or_notes: Older A. cumanensis usage is explicitly 'of authors, not Kunth', not an unconditional synonym

records.flora_original_name: Ambrosia trifida L. var. texana Scheele

flora_morphology.habit: Coarse annual with often red sap; stems 1–3(–5) m
flora_morphology.leaves: Usually opposite, petiolate; palmately 3(–5)-lobed, uppermost occasionally unlobed; both faces scabrous, especially upper
flora_morphology.fruits: Burr-like fruits ca. 4 mm, obovoid, with 4–8 small to obsolete tubercles

disagreements_or_notes: 1999 flora describes var. texana, whereas current inventory uses species A. trifida; do not assume all species-level material has identical varietal characters
Existing learner says 4–5 spines; flora states 4–8 small/obsolete tubercles

flora_morphology.habit: Hispid-pubescent perennial from branched woody root; stems 10–50 cm
flora_morphology.leaves: Genus: alternate with narrowed petiolar bases, linear to oblong-oblanceolate, entire to pinnately lobed
flora_morphology.heads: Numerous, large, long-peduncled; involucral height 4.5–6.2 mm, width 9–14 mm
flora_morphology.rays: Usually 40–85 rays by key (sometimes 25 at second flowering); white ligules 7–10 mm
flora_morphology.habitat: Rocky or sandy ground, chiefly limestone

disagreements_or_notes: Ray counts and root morphology from genus key must remain distinguished from species paragraph

flora_morphology.leaves: Basal blades elliptic/ovate, 5–15+ × 2–8 cm, entire or rarely toothed, thick, with 7–9 prominent longitudinal converging nerves; upper alternate stem leaves few and much smaller
flora_morphology.fruits: Achenes 4–5 mm; pappus numerous slender bristles

disagreements_or_notes: Flora cites Cacalia plantaginea as historical synonym; distinguish from A. ovatum with lanceolate leaves and unkeeled phyllaries
